stops.stop: Beauvais, the Hôtel de Ville and the Bourse Chevalier
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction. The award of the Bourse Chevalier on 24 May 1889 comes from printed municipal council deliberations reported by the director of the Oise departmental archives in 1991; the 1889 register itself was not located, and the original scholarship dossiers were destroyed in the bombing of Beauvais in June 1940. stops.stop: Paris, what the integral turned out to be for
stops.date_confidence: The Wiener claim is attested (en.wikipedia, 'Henri Lebesgue'): in 1947 Norbert Wiener argued that Lebesgue's integral had unexpected but important implications for the foundations Willard Gibbs laid under statistical mechanics. The original Wiener text was not checked. The abstraction of Lebesgue's measure into general spaces by Frechet, Daniell, Radon and Caratheodory is carried from the research dossier and not independently verified. Month and day default to January; the pin is the canonical Paris pin, this stop marking the afterlife of a body of work rather than a place anyone stood.

stops.stop: Beauvais, the street, and the crater
stops.date_confidence: The rue Henri Lebesgue in Beauvais is confirmed by OpenStreetMap geocoding at 49.42025, 2.07941; the date of the naming is not established anywhere reached, and 1975 is a bare placeholder with month and day defaulted. The lunar crater Lebesgue, 11.39 km across at 5.14 S 88.97 E on the far side, was approved by the IAU in 1976 (USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, feature 3323). Asteroid 26908 Lebesgue, provisional designation 1996 GK, was discovered on 11 April 1996 by P. G. Comba at Prescott (NASA/JPL Small-Body Database).

stops.stop: Rennes, the plaque and the centre
stops.date_confidence: The plaque to Henri-Leon Lebesgue at 4 rue Pongerard in Rennes is attested by a photograph of 21 May 2023 on Wikimedia Commons; the plaque itself is undated. The Centre Henri Lebesgue exists and, by its own site at lebesgue.fr, federates mathematics across six cities in western France including Rennes, Nantes, Brest, Angers and Le Mans; the founding year of 2012 is not stated by that site nor by the Wikipedia page cited for it in the research pool, so it is reconstruction and is used here only to order the stop. The Annales Henri Lebesgue, owned by the ENS Rennes and hosted by Centre Mersenne, carries no confirmed volume-one year: the 2018 usually given rests on a copyright line.
